The emer- gence of such ecosystems takes place over a period of time. Among the economies across the world, India oc- cupies a unique place as an emerging economy, ac- counting for the third highest concentration of technology startups and startup exits globally. In India, Bangalore has been attracting global attention increas- ingly, and more recently, as a hub of technology star- tups. Hyderabad, as one of the fast-emerging technology startup hubs in India, is closely following Bangalore. Given this, two questions are answered in this article: How did the entrepreneurial ecosystems of these two cities emerge over a period of time? and What is the structure of these ecosystems and what are their components? The seeds for the emergence of the two ecosystems were sown immediately after India’s independence in 1947 for Bangalore and after accession into Indian Uni- on in 1948 for Hyderabad. Public policy driven central public sector undertakings, public R&D institutions, educational institutions, supplemented by domestic private enterprises led both the cities to emerge as mod- ern industrial clusters. This was followed by the entry of multinational corporations in the information techno- logy and biotechnology industries in response to eco- nomic liberalization (in Bangalore) and in response to regional government initiatives (in Hyderabad), which resulted in the emergence of information techno- logy/biotechnology clusters. Subsequently, a steady lib- eralization of foreign investment rules and regulations encouraged a steady entry of R&D affiliates of multina- tional corporations in Bangalore, followed by in Hy- derabad, which nurtured clusters of R&D centres. It is the successive addition of these three different but inter-related clusters that gradually and steadily led to the rise of various components of entrepreneurial eco- systems in the two cities with a strong base of govern- ment–industry–academia triple helix model. Today, the entrepreneurial ecosystems of both Ban- galore and Hyderabad have all the critical components that have been commonly identified in empirical literat- ure in the international context. In addition, the diverse stakeholders of the two ecosystems enabled us to define the structure of an ecosystem in the Indian con- text. The triple helix model comprising government, in- dustry, and academia formed the foundation of the ecosystem, within which the system involved a nucleus comprising technology startups and prospective tech- nology startups with two outer layers. The first outer lay- er consisted of five primary (indispensable) factors (namely, finance, market, human resources, mentors, and support systems), whereas the outer-most layer comprised three secondary (supplementary) factors of culture, media and weather (in the case of Bangalore), culture and media (in the case of Hyderabad). However, the ways the triple helix model operates in the two cities are different. Whereas in the Bangalore eco- system, the triple helix interactions appear to have graduated from a “statist” model to a “laissez-faire” model and further to a “balanced” triple helix model, in the Hyderabad ecosystem, a “statist” model seems to be relevant even today. This is primarily because industry and academia have emerged, over a period of time, to be as important as the government, if not more, in Ban- galore. But government continues to be the dominant partner in Hyderabad even today, due to its pro-active ecosystem promotional policies. This has been corrob- orated by our interviewed stakeholders in both the cit- ies. But what does it imply? Broadly, an ecosystem for startups is assumed to gradu- ate through four different stages of evolution: i) nascent, ii) evolving, iii) mature, and iv) self-sustainable (Cukier et al., 2016). Considering that the vibrancy of both Ban- galore and Hyderabad ecosystems is largely confined to a rapidly growing “emergence of technology startups”, followed by a number of “stably operating” startups but with few “successful and grown” startups, it would be appropriate to conclude that these two ecosystems are still “evolving”, and therefore, have only “moderately matured”. Recently, in terms of the growth index for startup hubs, Bangalore has been ranked at the top in- ternationally, followed by London and Tel Aviv (Velay- anikal, 2015). The balanced triple helix model would prove beneficial to take Bangalore further towards ma- turity in the coming years. But the same cannot be as- sumed to happen in the case of Hyderabad. Only the continued active involvement of the government might ensure its further evolution towards maturity. In other words, any withdrawal or reduction in the role of the government might affect the further evolution of the Hy- derabad ecosystem towards maturity. Given the above, what are the key lessons/insights that we can derive from the experiences of Bangalore and Hyderabad for elsewhere in India and the world? The findings of our analysis yield three important lessons. First, the evolution of an entrepreneurial ecosystem in a technologically vibrant innovation cluster (Bangalore, which is often compared with a developed economy Technology Innovation Management Review July 2017 (Volume 7, Issue 7) 60 www.timreview.ca About the Author M H Bala Subrahmanya is a Professor of Economics in the Department of Management Studies at the In- dian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore, India. He joined Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore as an Assistant Professor in 1996, was promoted to Associ- ate Professor in 2002, and further to a Professor in 2008. He has more than 27 years of professional ex- perience, of which more than 21 years are at the IISc. During his professional career, he received a Commonwealth Fellowship (1999–2000), a Japan Foundation Fellowship (2004/2005), and a Fulbright- Nehru Senior Research Fellowship (2009/2010). He holds a PhD in Economics from the Institute for So- cial & Economic Change (ISEC) in Bangalore, and his field of specialization is Industrial Economics. Comparing the Entrepreneurial Ecosystems for Technology Startups in India M H Bala Subrahmanya cluster) and an emerging innovation cluster (Hydera- bad) within an emerging economy (India) is historically explored and analyzed. The critical factors that led to the laying of an ecosystem foundation gradually and steadily over a period of almost six decades in three dif- ferent phases, along with other supportive factors are brought out. This finding clearly demonstrates that eco- system development is an evolving process. But, this process will neither evolve naturally nor can it be built by design. As argued by Isenberg (2011), ecosystems are usually the result of intelligent evolution (a process that blends the invisible hand of markets and the deliberate helping hand of public policies). Second, an entrepreneurial ecosystem is essentially re- gional in character. The present study has revealed the unique features and elements involved in the develop- ment of the Bangalore and Hyderabad ecosystems. An entrepreneurial ecosystem is unique as it is the result of multiple elements interacting in highly complex and idiosyncratic ways, as brought out by these two cases. Though the Bangalore and Hyderabad ecosystems have some similarities, they are not identical. This finding highlights that it is neither feasible nor desirable to rep- licate either Bangalore or Hyderabad, even within India. What is essential is to ascertain and understand the structure and critical components of an entrepreneurial ecosystem, without which an ecosystem might not emerge, even if it emerges it may not survive, and even if it survives it may not prove to be effective or successful. Third, the structure and critical components of Ban- galore and Hyderabad entrepreneurial ecosystems are ascertained. The triple helix comprising government, in- dustry, and academia form the basis for an entrepren- eurial ecosystem as it supports or generates the critical components of an entrepreneurial ecosystem. An entre- preneurial ecosystem for technology startups is defined as a structure with the triple helix as the base, and it comprises a nucleus (startup entrepreneurs and pro- spective entrepreneurs) with two outer layers consisting of some core and indispensable components as the first outer layer, which include: i) financiers (in the form of seed funds, angel investors, venture capitalists, and private equity firms), ii) markets, iii) human resources, iv) nurturers (in the form of accelerators, business in- cubators, and co-working spaces), and v) business and technology mentors. The second outer layer consists of supplementary factors such as supportive culture, ef- fective media, and, if possible, good weather. Thus, the nucleus and the core components, supplemented ad- equately by the secondary factors, and with the triple helix as the base, define the structure of an ecosystem for technology startups. Their adequate and growing presence and interactions will generate vibrancy in the ecosystem for its further growth. This would lead to an increasing scale of technology startup emergence, nur- turing for survival and stability, and growth of the suc- cessful ones, thereby contributing to national economic growth, innovation achievements, and em- ployment generation. View Measuring an Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Article Full-text available * Jan 2015 * Jordan Bell-Masterson * Dane Stangler How do you measure your entrepreneurial ecosystem? How should you interpret the data about your startup community? What economic indicators should matter for vibrancy and growth? These questions come up repeatedly in conversations with entrepreneurs, program heads, event organizers, investors, policymakers, and others. The frequency of these queries reflects the phenomenon: With the rapid spread of efforts to build entrepreneurial ecosystems, it’s only natural to wonder what outcomes should be tracked. And, what you track depends on what you’re trying to achieve.In some places, the desired outcome is simply more: more entrepreneurs, more companies, and more jobs. Other communities design their ecosystem efforts around a particular type of company or type of job. Some regions, moreover, see the “entrepreneurial ecosystem” as a marketing effort, and focus on a particular type of individual they hope to attract to their area. For other cities, the only thing that matters is the “exit” - initial public offerings and acquisitions. These are all worthy objectives, and communities must define their own goals. Yet where most places fail is in reliance on a handful of limited input metrics rather than outcomes. To judge the vibrancy of their entrepreneurial ecosystems, many states and regions focus on things like research and development funding at universities, available investment capital, and engineering degrees. These may be associated with more entrepreneurial activity, but they are inputs, not necessarily the outcomes to be tracked. Other regions focus on patents or technology licenses out of universities - these are a piece of the puzzle, but they’re not necessarily the leading indicators of entrepreneurial vibrancy. At the other end of the spectrum is the kitchen-sink approach - because every part of an entrepreneurial ecosystem is critically important, you must track everything. This approach has the admirable quality of avoiding Campbell’s Law but provides no sense of prioritization or focus for those community leaders involved in the ecosystem. There must be some middle ground between trying to capture every dimension of an entrepreneurial ecosystem and overly focusing on only one or two indicators. There are also different levels of measurement for entrepreneurial ecosystems. In this paper, we focus on the overall performance of the ecosystem in terms of outcomes and vibrancy. In future work, we will explore measurement indicators that can be instituted at the level of programs and organizations. applications.content: 🚨Bengaluru's Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology to be designed by architects behind Grand Egyptian Museum Bengaluru is a step closer to getting India's first museum dedicated to innovation, startups and technology, with the Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology (MIST) appointing the Heneghan Peng Architects-led consortium as its Design and Technical Agency (DTA). The project, being developed by NGO UnboxingBLR in partnership with the Karnataka government's Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology (ITBT), will come up at the repurposed NGEF campus in Byappanahalli. Read More: https://lnkd.in/dBSDsbF5 To view or add a comment, sign in * 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗳𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹. 𝗧𝘄𝗼 𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗽𝘀. 𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: What happens when lab-born innovation meets design? We found out this weekend at the WDC Campus Festival. 👇 The setting: the Museum Angewandte Kunst, the World Design Capital Frankfurt RheinMain 2026, and its exhibition "dreams, ideas & prototypes." A room full of designers, students, researchers and the plainly curious — not your usual startup crowd. Which made it the perfect place to ask that question. Proof that a material born in a lab can end up in your hands. 🧵 Smarfecto (formerly AlsterrLab) — engineering the yarn itself, not just coating the fabric, to build textiles that work for preventive health. No electronics, no batteries — just smart material science. 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝘂𝗰𝗸 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗺𝗲: At a design festival, "design" turned out to be the most natural bridge of all. The surface, the feel, the trust it takes to get a brand to say yes to something new — that's design as much as it's business. Both founders made that case better than any slide ever could. Thanks to Montgomery Wagner (revoltech) and Essak Khan (Smarfecto) and Thomas Glaser (Futury) for sharing so openly, and to the whole WDC Campus team (Georg-Christof Bertsch, Roland Lambrette & Co.) — for the invitation and a genuinely great weekend. More of this, please. 👀 #WDC2026 #WorldDesignCapital #Futury #Startups #Design #Innovation #Sustainability #Spinoff To view or add a comment, sign in * A landmark moment for Karnataka's innovation journey. The consortium led by heneghan peng architects — the team behind the Grand Egyptian Museum has been selected to design India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology (MIST) and Innoverse, our upcoming deep-tech innovation hub. Selected through a rigorous global Quality and Cost-Based Selection process involving 13 international consortiums, this marks a defining step in Karnataka's vision to build world-class institutions celebrating India's innovation story. Located on the historic NGEF campus, Bengaluru: MIST will preserve and showcase India's startup, technology & innovation journey and INNOVERSE (Govt. of Karnataka) will nurture the next generation of entrepreneurs, researchers and deep-tech innovators. Phase 1 opens in 2028. Bengaluru has long been India's innovation capital. MIST and Innoverse will cement that legacy for generations to come. #Karnataka #MIST #Innoverse #ITBTGoK #StartupKarnataka #BengaluruInnovation A proud moment for Bengaluru and Karnataka. The consortium of Heneghan Peng, Cadence and DROO Architects has been selected to design the Museum of Innovation and Start‑Up Technology in Bengaluru. Led by Heneghan Peng—architects of the Grand Egyptian Museum—alongside long‑time collaborators DROO and Cadence, the team brings complementary strengths and a unified vision. Together, they aim to create not just a museum but a new civic institution for Bengaluru: one that celebrates ingenuity, supports entrepreneurship, preserves technological heritage and inspires future generations to shape India’s innovation story Chosen through a rigorous global Quality and Cost-Based Selection process involving 13 international consortiums, this marks a significant milestone in our vision to build world-class institutions that celebrate India’s innovation journey while shaping its future. Located at the historic NGEF campus, MIST will preserve and showcase the story of India’s startup, technology and innovation ecosystem, while Innoverse will foster the next generation of entrepreneurs, researchers and deep-tech innovators. “Congratulations to the winning consortium and thank every participating global team for their exceptional proposals. My appreciation also goes to the jury, KTIMF, UnboxingBLR, the Department of Electronics, IT, BT & S&T, BRMA and all our partners who have worked tirelessly to bring this vision closer to reality,” said Mr Priyank Kharge. “Bengaluru has long been India’s innovation capital. With MIST and Innoverse, we are creating institutions that will inspire future generations, celebrate our journey, and reinforce Karnataka’s position as a global leader in technology and innovation. Phase 1 is expected to open in 2028, and I look forward to seeing this vision come to life,”said Mr Prashanth Prakash. applications.title: India's First Startup Museum to Launch in Bengaluru by 2027 | AIM posted on the topic | LinkedIn
applications.content: Bengaluru is preparing to launch India’s first startup and tech museum by 2027, with officials and industry leaders reviewing the vision for what will become a global-standard archive of Indian innovation. At the meeting, leaders from Biocon, Infosys, BIAL, Mercedes-Benz R&D, Strand Life Sciences, and Metri joined senior government officials Manjula N and Rahul Chanapankar to shape how NGF’s historic switchgear facility will be transformed into a 12,000 m² landmark for technology and entrepreneurship. The discussion highlighted plans for immersive exhibits capturing the rise of India’s tech ecosystem, from Flipkart’s first office to ISRO’s PSLV story and early breakthroughs from Infosys and Biocon. With phase one set for 2027 and phase two for 2028, the museum is envisioned as both a living memory of India’s technological journey and a launchpad that inspires future innovators. Watch the complete episode on Front Page by AIM - https://lnkd.in/gkzfbU6q ## More Relevant Posts * From #Lab-to-#Life to #Prototype-to-#Product | Global Media Delegation in #Bengaluru As #globalattention turns toward #deeptech, #lifesciences, and #advancedmanufacturing, #Karnataka continues to demonstrate how #researchled #innovation translates into #realworldoutcomes. Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) recently hosted an #internationaldelegation of #journalists across two of Bengaluru’s core #innovationhubs - Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) and ARTgarage (ARTPARK @ Indian Institute of Science (IISc))—offering a direct view of how #innovation is supported from #discovery to #deployment. At C-CAMP, the focus was on #deepscience translation across #healthcare, #agriculture, and #environmentalinnovation. The ecosystem has already delivered: \* 600+ startups supported across life sciences and deep science domains \* $14M+ deployed through grants and investments to catalyse innovation \* 100+ products already in the market \* $1.6B+ cumulative valuation of C-CAMP-supported startups The delegation also saw how #globallicensing, #industrypartnerships, and advanced platforms #accelerate #solutions in #diagnostics, #digitalhealth, #agribiotech, #sepsis mitigation, and #antimicrobial resistance. At ARTgarage (ARTPARK @ IISc), the emphasis shifted to #productengineering and #manufacturingreadiness. Founders demonstrated #autonomousrobotics and advanced #hardwaresystems already in testing and #earlymarketvalidation, supported by: \* Shared testbeds and manufacturing infrastructure lowering entry barriers \* Reduced time-to-prototype and time-to-market for robotics, AI, and autonomous systems \* A clear pathway from R&D to scalable products Together, C-CAMP and ARTgarage reflect #Karnataka’s end-to-end deep-tech ecosystem—connecting #research, #translation, #prototyping, #manufacturing, and #marketaccess. For #founders, #investors, and #partners in #biotech, #healthtech, #agriinnovation, #robotics, #AI, and #advancedmanufacturing, Karnataka offers #structuredprograms, #pilotopportunities, and #ecosystempartnerships through KDEM. 📩 Stay connected with our teams for upcoming delegations, sector-led engagements, and collaboration opportunities! Contact: Samir Venugopal - samir.venugopal@karnatakadigital.in Ishita Gupta - ishita.gupta@karnatakadigital.in #karnataka #deeptech #innovationecosystem #biotech #healthtech #agritech #robotics #advancedmanufacturing #startupindia #makeinindia #kdem Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (BRIC-inStem) To view or add a comment, sign in * The IIT Kharagpur Research Park had the honour of welcoming T. V. Narendran, Chairman of the Board of Governors, Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, and Managing Director & CEO of Tata Steel. His visit highlighted the critical role of industry–academia collaboration in advancing India’s deep-tech and innovation ecosystem. A key highlight was Mr. Narendran’s interaction with Senrysa, a deep-tech IT and applied AI company operating from the Research Park. During his visit to Senrysa’s R&D wing, discussions focused on ongoing joint R&D initiatives between IIT Kharagpur and Senrysa, reflecting a strong model of research-led industrial collaboration. Among the focus areas showcased was HealthTech, particularly point-of-care diagnostic solutions being jointly developed under the leadership of Suman Chakraborty, Director, Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. Mr. Narendran appreciated the potential of these innovations to deliver affordable, scalable healthcare solutions for rural and semi-urban India, especially across Eastern India—closely aligned with his vision of inclusive, impact-driven industrial growth. Senrysa also demonstrated its broader deep-tech capabilities, including: -Computer vision and AI-driven analytics -Mission-grade AI systems -End-to-end platforms designed for real-world, large-scale deployment These demonstrations reinforced Senrysa’s role as a bridge between academic research and scalable product development, exemplifying effective academia–industry partnership. In his interactions with startup leaders at the Research Park, the Chairman emphasised the need for stronger industry engagement, improved access to capital, and structured pathways to build globally competitive companies from Kolkata. He highlighted companies like Senrysa as critical enablers in translating research excellence into market-ready solutions. Senrysa’s Managing Director, Kumar P. Saha, reaffirmed his deep personal commitment to strengthening academia–industry collaboration, underscoring Senrysa’s long-term vision of translating cutting-edge research into scalable, mission-grade innovations with real societal impact. The visit concluded on a positive and forward-looking note. Though at a formative stage, the IIT Kharagpur Research Park is rapidly emerging as a key hub for deep-tech innovation, entrepreneurship, and technology-led impact from Eastern India, contributing meaningfully to Viksit Bharat through indigenous, scalable innovation. ImagiNXT 2026 partnering with the National Innovation Foundation – India is a powerful signal that grassroots innovators will now share the same spotlight as deep-tech founders, global brands, and policy leaders. From frugal solutions that solve local challenges to scalable technologies that can travel the world, this is how “India innovates for India – and the world.” ImagiNXT 2026 is being built as India’s Festival of Technology and Innovation – a global platform where 15,000+ attendees, 1,000+ startups, 300+ investors, and 200+ tech brands come together to imagine what’s next. Naxatra Labs, the Ahmedabad-based startup specializing in high-efficiency electric motors, has successfully raised \*\*$3 million in a Pre-Series A round\*\* led by Rainmatter. 🌱 This round saw participation from industry leaders including Mohit Tandon (Delhivery), Vijay Shekhar Sharma (Paytm), Aloke Bajpai (ixigo), and other prominent founders and operators. Over the past four years, Naxatra Labs has built strong R&D capabilities, moving multiple products from concept to commercial production. Their focus spans electromagnetic design, validation, and manufacturing processes, positioning them as a key player in India’s energy transition ecosystem ⚡. 💡 Vishvesh Krishna from Rainmatter by Zerodha highlighted their commitment to backing founders solving complex engineering challenges, while Himanshu Aggarwal (Giraffe Studios) described this as their first deeptech energy transition investment. applications.content: Bengaluru will host India’s first startup and technology museum by 2027, according to an announcement by the Karnataka government. The project, spread across 12,000 square meters, will be built inside a repurposed Switch Gear factory shed on the NGEF campus in Baiyappanahalli. The museum is being developed through a public-private partnership between the Department of Electronics, IT & BT and S&T, and UnboxingBLR, under the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF). The development will take place in two phases. applications.title: Karnataka to Launch Innovation Museum, AI University, Boost Startups
applications.content: # Karnataka to Launch Innovation Museum, AI University, Boost Startups x Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge announces MIST, AI University, and increased funding for deep-tech startups. The state aims to lead in AI and innovation. Bengaluru, July 24 (PTI) Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge on Friday announced a slew of initiatives, including the launch of MIST (Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology), the Innovers Foundation, enhanced funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, a proposed AI University, and the Nipuna Karnataka skilling programme, ahead of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS). The summit will be held from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) under the theme 'AI & Beyond', the Minister who holds the Information Technology, Biotechnology and Home portfolios, said. The minister also announced the constitution of a Deep Tech Working Group, a Government First policy to make government datasets available to startups through a regulatory sandbox, and said Karnataka would continue to position itself as the country's leading destination for artificial intelligence and deep-tech innovation. "AI may be the current buzzword, but Karnataka has always led emerging technologies and will continue to lead the next phase of artificial intelligence. BTS will serve as a platform for policy discussions, strategic decisions and the preparation of a blueprint not only for Karnataka but also for the country," Kharge told reporters. Kharge said the government has launched the Innovers Foundation to mentor revenue-generating deep-tech startups, help them access global markets and facilitate the adoption of their innovations by the government through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. Reiterating that the next decade would be Karnataka's "Deep Tech Decade", he said the government has doubled funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, increasing the maximum grant from Rs 50 lakh to Rs one crore. He said 983 applications were received, from which 33 deep-tech startups were selected and awarded grants totalling Rs 33 crore. Of these, 24 startups are from Bengaluru, one each from Hoskote, Udupi, Bidar and Hubballi, while five are from Delhi, Maharashtra and Telangana. "What is particularly encouraging is that 12 of the 33 startups are women-led," Kharge said, adding that grants ranged from Rs 85 lakh to Rs one crore. The minister also announced the formation of a Deep Tech Working Group/Vision Group, led by industry representatives, to strengthen Karnataka's deep-tech ecosystem. Announcing MIST, Kharge said part of the old NGF factory premises in Bengaluru would be transformed into India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology at an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model. He said the project would preserve the heritage factory structure and would be designed by Dublin-based architectural firm Heneghan Peng, known for designing the Grand Egyptian Museum. Kharge said the proposed Government First policy would allow startups and companies to access government datasets and public digital infrastructure through a regulatory sandbox, with the government becoming the first customer for viable solutions developed using public data. He also announced plans to establish a state-of-the-art AI University, developed in partnership with industry, think tanks and private companies, to focus on skilling, upskilling, research and development, incubation and global collaborations. Drawing a parallel with the Indian Institute of Science, Kharge said the proposed AI University would create a globally competitive ecosystem for artificial intelligence, adding that a detailed blueprint would be ready within 15 to 20 days. Addressing concerns over AI-led job disruptions, the minister said the government was rolling out Nipuna Karnataka, which he described as India's largest reskilling and upskilling programme, with an outlay of over Rs 300 crore. He said the industry-led programme aims to ensure 70 per cent placement and 100 per cent employability, equipping professionals with skills needed in emerging technologies as automation and artificial intelligence reshape the workforce. Kharge also said Karnataka was finalising a framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in governance and was preparing a Sustainable Data Centre Policy to promote environmentally sustainable technologies such as liquid cooling while ensuring future data centres have access to renewable energy and adequate water resources. Read More India’s technology industry is today pegged at $227 billion plus. It is time the country — the world’s software capital — built its own technology and innovation museum. Unsurprisingly, the country’s tech epicentre Bengaluru is hosting the endeavour. The city will soon house the country’s first Technology & Innovation Museum of India. Read Less Share Follow us BENGALURU: India’s technology industry is today pegged at $227 billion plus. It is time the country — the world’s software capital — built its own technology and innovation museum. Unsurprisingly, the country’s tech epicentre Bengaluru is hosting the endeavour. The city will soon house the country’s first Technology & Innovation Museum of India. Tired of too many ads?go ad free now The museum will serve as a one-stop destination to learn about India’s startup, technology and innovation journey. Expected to be built in the next 18- 24 months, the museum will be located at the NGEF site in Byappanahalli and will blend well with the upcoming tree park project in the vicinity. Envisaged with an initial corpus of Rs 100 crore, the museum will be a public-private partnership effort and showcase the nation’s strength and capabilities in the technology world. Exactly the way National Museum of India and The National Gallery of Modern Art in Delhi showcase India’s rich cultural heritage. In that sense, think of it as a museum built in Bengaluru but built for the country. While still at an early stage of conceptualisation, we have some clarity about the different thrust areas of the museum. In its representation, it will have three important foundational pillars. The first pillar will be that of technology and innovation coming out of government research labs, academic institutions like IISc and PSUs like Isro and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL). The second pillar will be that of corporates and large enterprises –—both domestic as well as MNCs — who have added both heft and capacity to the country’s technology and innovation landscape. And the third pillar will be of India’s vibrant and rapidly growing startup ecosystem. Chronologically, the museum will have three components — past, present and future. The future section will be dynamic and will undertake periodic thematic exploration, especially in areas where India is leading or is expected to lead the world and set the global agenda. Tired of too many ads?go ad free now Some of the areas that may be considered — biotech, urban tech, space tech, digital health, digital public goods like India Stack, urban and civic tech, and digitisation of global MNCs. The museum will also look at some cutting-edge work being undertaken by GCCs or global capability centres of MNCs in India. It will lean heavily on the latest digital tools and technologies — including holograms, haptic interactions and immersive environments using augmented and virtual reality — to create interactive experiences to engage the audience. Globally, leading tech hubs like Tel Aviv and Seattle have underlined their technology legacies through museums. Peres Centre for Peace and Innovation in Tel Aviv and Bezos Centre of Innovation in Seattle are great recent examples of building modern museums with highly interactive experiences. We hope our museum will add Bengaluru to this global list. It is also interesting to note that the Technology & Innovation Museum of India is being envisaged at a time when Bengaluru is seeing a spate of new museums being built both by the private sector as well in public-private partnership space. Tired of too many ads?go ad free now The Indian Music Experience Museum, built in 2019, is India’s first interactive music museum supported by the Brigade Group. Science Gallery Bengaluru — which aspires to bring science back into the culture — is currently being built as a private-public partnership. Finally, the latest addition to the list is MAP or Museum of Art and Photography in Bengaluru. MAP aspires to democratise art and make it an enjoyable and relevant experience. It is leveraging Bengaluru’s cutting-edge IT infrastructure to become one of the most technologically advanced museums not just in India but the world. It is creating experiences that will be augmented with digital interventions including the creation of immersive arts. For example, static paintings will be brought to life by creating animated and immersive stories. Tired of too many ads?go ad free now Interactive touch walls, AI-enabled interviews with holograms of artists like MF Hussain, sensor -based digital art views, etc are just some of the digital tools they are using. We look forward to building the tech and innovation museum with many more such tools. And we hope the museum will inspire innovation and entrepreneurship in the country and help showcase India’s compelling legacy in the technology world. *The writer is founding partner at venture capital firm Accel Partners and chairman, Karnataka Vision Group on Startups* *Stay updated with the latest news on Times of India. applications.title: Bengaluru To Host India’s First Startup And Technology Museum To Inspire Young Innovators: Pravin Hungund
applications.content: ETV Bharat / bharat # Bengaluru To Host India’s First Startup And Technology Museum To Inspire Young Innovators: Pravin Hungund ## In an exclusive interview with ETV Bharat, Pravin Hungund said the Startup and Technology Museum is aimed at inspiring next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs Technology Innovation Museum (ETV Bharat) By ETV Bharat English Team Published : December 19, 2025 at 5:59 PM IST 3 Min Read **By Mohammed Rafiq Mulla** **Bengaluru:**India’s first museum dedicated entirely to science, technology, and innovation is set to take shape in Bengaluru, reinforcing the city’s position as the country’s technology capital. The Startup and Technology Museum will be developed at the historic NGEF campus in Baiyappanahalli and aims to present India’s journey in science, innovation, and entrepreneurship in an accessible format. Speaking to ETV Bharat, Pravin Hungund, CEO of the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation, said the idea behind the museum is to fill a major gap in India’s cultural and educational landscape. “Bengaluru has over 30 museums, but none that document India’s technological story or its role in global innovation. This museum is meant to capture that journey, from government laboratories and academic institutions to startups and future technologies,” he said. Pravin Hungund, CEO of the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (ETV Bharat) According to Hungund, Bengaluru was the natural choice for such an initiative because of its long association with science, research, and technology-led growth. The museum is envisioned as a space that reflects both India’s achievements and its aspirations in emerging fields. **UnboxingBLR - The Public-Private Partnership Behind the Project** The Startup and Technology Museum is being developed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and Science and Technology, and UnboxingBLR with the state government holding a 49 percent stake. To implement the project, a Section 8 company named the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation has been established. Hungund said the PPP model has made it possible to combine public purpose with private expertise. “This structure allows the museum to function as a public learning platform while remaining flexible, contemporary, and connected to the innovation ecosystem,” he explained. The museum is part of a larger twin initiative that also includes Innoverse, a deep-tech incubator led by the Department of ITBT. Together, the two projects are expected to create a space where technological heritage, research, and entrepreneurship come together. Tech Innovation Museum in Bengaluru (ETV Bharat) **Reviving the NGEF Campus Through Adaptive Reuse** The museum and the Innoverse will be housed within a former switchgear factory shed at the NGEF campus, a site spread across 105 acres, with nearly 65 acres of green cover. Around 12,000 square metres have been earmarked for the museum, while another 11,000 square metres will be used for Innoverse. Hungund said the choice of location reflects a conscious effort to combine heritage conservation with sustainable development. “The NGEF factory is part of Bengaluru’s industrial history. By adapting it for a cultural and educational purpose, we are preserving that legacy while giving it a new role,” he said. The design will focus on creating a futuristic museum experience within a historic structure, making the site both functional and meaningful for visitors. **Inspiring Students and Young Entrepreneurs** A key focus of the Startup and Technology Museum is education and inspiration, particularly for students and young innovators. Hungund said the museum will go beyond static displays and textbooks. “This is a public space for learning and exploration. Visitors will walk through India’s technology story, from institutions like ISRO, DRDO, and IISc to startups and unicorns,” he said. The museum will feature permanent galleries, thematic exhibitions, interactive installations, and live programmes. Students will be able to engage with technologies such as artificial intelligence, robotics, space technology, and climate technology through participatory activities. Hungund emphasised that showcasing people and ideas behind innovations is central to the museum’s approach. “We want young visitors to see themselves as problem-solvers and entrepreneurs,” he said. The presence of Innoverse next door is expected to strengthen this vision. While the museum sparks curiosity, the incubator will provide mentorship, research support, and incubation opportunities. “The idea is to create a seamless path from curiosity to experimentation and, eventually, to real ventures,” Hungund added. Summing up the larger goal, Hungund described the museum as a collaborative effort to shape India’s technological future. “This initiative reflects a shared vision of how India’s innovation story can inspire the next generation,” he said. applications.content: # Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology # Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology The Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology (MIST) will be India’s first museum dedicated exclusively to chronicling modern India’s journey in innovation, technology, and entrepreneurship. Grounded in the present and oriented toward the future, the museum aims to capture the impact of transformations in India’s technology landscape and spark curiosity and dialogue across generations. Driven by the Karnataka Technology Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF), the project is built on a pioneering public–private partnership model between the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Government of Karnataka, and UnboxingBLR. MIST will be housed within one of the original switchgear factory sheds at the historic NGEF Campus, Baiyappanahalli, set within a 105-acre urban forest (65 acres of green cover). Through the adaptive reuse of the switchgear factory shed, its 10,061 sq. m. footprint can be expanded to nearly 24,000 sq. m., with additional floors and double-height volumes. Of this, approximately 12,325 sq. m. will be dedicated to the museum. The larger NGEF site is being developed independently by the Government of Karnataka as a cultural hub, and once realized, MIST will form an integral part of this broader cultural ecosystem. ## Vision To establish a world-class, landmark institution that captures modern India's extraordinary technological legacy, celebrates its present leadership in innovation, and inspires its future pioneers. ## Mission To create a dynamic ecosystem that demystifies technology, catalyzes research, and provides an immersive cultural and educational platform for all. ###### Team ## Board ## / ## Advisory Board ## / ## Team ## / ## Consultant Prashanth Prakash Chairperson KTIMF, Chairperson Vision Group - Startup & Co-founder UnboxingBLR Dr. Manjula. applications.content: ###### Home ###### / ###### Insights ###### / ###### Request for Proposals for Selection of Design & Technical Authority # Request for Proposals for Selection of Design & Technical Authority Jan 12, 2026 Request For Proposal Download Corrigendum-III here. **The Landmark Project: MIST & Innoverse** Bengaluru, India's Technology Capital, is set to welcome a pioneering cultural and scientific landmark. The Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology (MIST) will be the country's first museum dedicated exclusively to chronicling India's journey in science, technology, and entrepreneurship. Alongside it, Innoverse will operate as a government-led deep-tech incubator. Together, located within the historic NGEF Campus in Baiyappanahalli, they represent a transformative step in Karnataka's commitment to shaping the future of technology and making it accessible to the public. **Our Vision & Mission** **Vision:** To establish a world-class, landmark institution that captures India's extraordinary technological legacy, celebrates its present leadership in innovation, and inspires its future pioneers. **Mission:** To create a dynamic ecosystem—comprising a public museum (MIST) and a deep-tech incubator (Innoverse)—that demystifies technology, catalyzes research, and provides an immersive cultural and educational platform for all. **A Unique Partnership Model** This project is built on a pioneering partnership model: * MIST is being developed as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Department of Electronics , Information Technology and Biotechnology, Government of Karnataka (49%) and UnboxingBLR (51%). It is governed by the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF), a dedicated Section 8 company. * Innoverse is a 100% Government of Karnataka (ITBT Department) initiative. It will operate under the Innoverse Foundation, an independent Section 8 company, focusing on research, development, and startup incubation. UnboxingBLR is the Lead Sponsor for MIST and is also managing the combined selection process for the Design and Technical Agency for both projects. **The Site: A Symbol of Regeneration** MIST and Innoverse will be housed within one of the original Switch Gear Factory Sheds at the historic NGEF Campus, set within a 105-acre urban forest (65 acres of green cover). This ambitious adaptive-reuse initiative is one of India's most significant cultural infrastructure projects, symbolizing the regeneration of industrial heritage for a knowledge-based future. **Site Specifications:** * **Building:** Existing shed with ground floor and basement, internal heights up to 13 meters. * **Footprint:** Approximately 10,061 sq. m., expandable to nearly 24,000 sq. m. with additional floors. * **Allocated Space:** ~12,325 sq. m. for MIST and ~11,765 sq. m. for Innoverse. **Phased Development & Governance** The project will be realized in two clear phases: * **Phase 1** + **Museum Development Stage:** Building architecture with finishes & half of permanent galleries. + **Timeline:** Late 2027 + **Budget:** INR 200 Crores (for both MIST + Innoverse) * **Phase 2** + **Museum Development Stage:** Completion of remaining galleries including exhibit fabrication and development + **Timeline:** Late 2028 + **Budget:** INR 45 Crores **Project Team:** * **UnboxingBLR:** Lead Sponsor. Responsible for project planning, fundraising, budget management, and appointment of consultants. * **Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF):** The governing Section 8 company. **CEO: Mr. Pravin Hungund.** Also, **CEO (In Charge)**, **Innoverse Foundation**. * **Museum & Cultural Planners (Batul Raaj Mehta & Associates - BRMA LLP):** Responsible for institutional vision, governance model, and running the selection process for the Design and Technical Agency (DTA). **Curatorial Approach: A Collaborative Mode** MIST aims to interpret, demystify, and celebrate technology. It will adopt a distributed, expert-led curatorial model to ensure authenticity * Structured consultations with board members, stakeholders, and domain experts. * Contributions from research groups, history societies, and industry specialists. * Guidance from an international Curatorial Advisory Board of futurists, science communicators, academics, and museum professionals. * This collaborative process will define gallery themes, exhibition narratives, and immersive public programs. As part of Project Phase 1, an RFP for selecting the Design & Technical Agency (DTA) has been issued, inviting leading architectural and exhibition design teams from India and overseas. **Issuing Authority** On behalf of the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF) Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Government of Karnataka & UnboxingBLR ###### RFP documents will be downloaded as a ZIP file. applications.title: Karnataka to Launch India's First Startup and Innovation Museum
applications.content: # Karnataka to Launch India's First Startup and Innovation Museum By siliconindia | Saturday, 25 July 2026, 04:45 Hrs Karnataka has announced plans to build India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology (MIST) in Bengaluru with an investment of Rs 300 crore. The state also unveiled several new initiatives, including the Innoverse Foundation, higher grants for deep-tech startups, and a proposed AI University ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. Karnataka is set to establish India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology (MIST) in Bengaluru with an investment of Rs 300 crore under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. The project aims to celebrate innovation, entrepreneurship, and technological progress while strengthening the state's position as India's leading startup hub. The announcement was made by Karnataka Minister for Home, Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Priyank Kharge, ahead of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), which will take place from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC). This year's summit will be held under the theme 'AI & Beyond.' The museum will be developed at the repurposed Switchgear Factory Shed located in the NGEF campus in Bengaluru. It will be jointly developed by the UnboxingBLR Foundation and the Karnataka Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology. For the project, the government has selected the Henegan Peng Architects consortium, the global architecture firm known for designing the Grand Egyptian Museum. Along with the museum, the Karnataka government announced several initiatives aimed at strengthening the state's innovation ecosystem. These include the launch of the Innoverse Foundation, an increase in grants for deep-tech startups under the Elevate Next program, and a proposal to establish an AI University. Under the updated Elevate Next program, eligible deep-tech startups can now receive grants of up to Rs 1 crore, a move expected to support innovation in emerging technologies. Speaking about the Innoverse Foundation, Kharge said it is a state government initiative created to position Karnataka as a global DeepTech hub. Priyank Kharge, says, "Innoverse acts as a catalyst, mentoring successful revenue-generating deep-tech Startups to evolve from good product-market fit to industry dominance. The Foundation empowers the next generation of industry leaders by providing critical market access, access to essential capital, and expert mentorship" . The foundation is designed to help deep-tech startups scale beyond the early growth stage by connecting them with investors, industry experts, and new market opportunities. It will also focus on helping startups build sustainable businesses with global potential. The proposed AI University is another key initiative announced ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit. The university is expected to support research, talent development, and industry collaboration in artificial intelligence, further strengthening Karnataka's leadership in advanced technologies. With these initiatives, the state government aims to create a stronger ecosystem for startups, encourage innovation, and attract global investments across sectors such as artificial intelligence, deep technology, and advanced manufacturing. The Bengaluru Tech Summit is expected to serve as a platform for showcasing these initiatives while bringing together policymakers, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers, and technology leaders from around the world. Through projects like MIST and Innoverse, Karnataka is looking to reinforce its reputation as one of the country's most active centers for technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship.

applications.content: E-PAPER DH x * India * Karnataka * DH Specials * Opinion * World * Business * Sports * Video * Entertainment ADVERTISEMENT Homeindiakarnatakabengaluru Bengaluru to get India's first startup, tech museum by 2027Spread across 12,000 sqm within the repurposed Switch Gear factory shed on the NGEF campus in Baiyappanahalli, the museum is being developed as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Department of Electronics, IT&BT and S&T, and UnboxingBLR. Asra Mavad Last Updated 02 December 2025, 04:35 IST Follow Us Representative image for Indian startups. Credit: iStock Images Bengaluru: Bengaluru is set to house India’s first startup and tech museum by 2027. ADVERTISEMENT Spread across 12,000 sqm within the repurposed Switch Gear factory shed on the NGEF campus in Baiyappanahalli, the museum is being developed as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Department of Electronics, IT&BT and S&T, and UnboxingBLR. It will be developed under the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF). The museum space will be developed in two phases. The first phase is set to go live in 2027, said Prashanth Prakash, co-founder and chairperson of UnboxingBLR, with the second phase expected to take off a year later. The museum aims to highlight India’s history of innovation, science and technology, with Bengaluru at the centre of it all, said Prakash. “I believe that a lot of economic contributions have materially changed the trajectory of our country in the last 25 years has been tech-led and digital, and central to that are also the entrepreneurial contributions of Bengaluru. We’ll be chronicling the last four to five decades of technological advancements. There is no better place than Bengaluru to showcase that,” he told DH. In addition to what has transpired, the museum will also provide perspective and insights into what the future holds. A global Request for Proposal (RFP) for the museum’s design is expected to go out in the next 30 days. An approximate budget of Rs 100 crore has been allocated to design and build the museum, which has been in the talks for the past three years. “We’re calling on startups and companies from across the country who’d like to be a part of the museum. Leaning heavily on the latest technology, it is going to be an interactive space, so there’s lots of room for experimentation,” added Prakash. A board of industry leaders has been set up to aid the launch of the museum. The board will be chaired by Prakash, and it consists of Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Infosys cofounder Kris Gopalakrishnan, Managing Director and CEO of Bangalore International Airport Limited Hari Marar, Ajit Abraham Isaac of Quess Corp, Manu Ramchandra Saale of Mercedes-Benz R&D, Vijay Chandru of Strand Life Sciences, and Krishnakumar Natarajan of Mindtree. The government officials, such as IT&BT secretary Manjula N and IAS Rahul Sharanappa Sankaur, will also be involved in the development of the interactive space. The museum will be situated near Innoverse, a state government-backed deep-tech incubator initiative. About 11,000 sqm have been allocated for the Innoverse project. applications.content: ## Advanced Search ## Export Query Syntax | | | | --- | --- | | Query Name: | | | Search Run Date: | | | Search Result Count: | | | Query Syntax: | | save as csv ## SEARCH TIPS for text fields #### Boolean searches Use the boolean operators **AND**, **OR**, and **NOT** to narrow or broaden your search results. By default, an AND relationship is assumed between Search Within terms unless you specify a different operator in the **Edit Query:** input. By default, an **OR** relationship is assumed between words within 1 Search Within term. #### Searching for phrases Enclose your search terms within **double** quotation marks (" ") to search for an exact match of that phrase. If no quotation marks are used, search results will be populated with publications that contain your search terms somewhere in the text. For example, if you search for *"machine learning"* the search engine will limit the results to publications that contain this exact phrase otherwise an **OR** will be assumed in between the words. Curly quotes (“ ”) are also acceptable eg. *“machine learning”* **NOTE 1:** opening and closing quotes must be of the same type; curly or straight. Please avoid entering *“machine learning"* **NOTE 2:** single quotation marks (' ') are ignored and will not return exact phrase matches. #### Wildcards Use an asterisk (\*) to specify any number of unknown characters. For example, if you search for **comput\***, the search engine will provide results that contain words such as compute, comput**ation**, comput**ing**, etc. Use a question mark (?) to specify any single unknown character. For example, if you search for **compute?**, the search engine will provide results that contain words such as computer or compute**d** but not compute**rs** because the question mark represents only one character. **NOTE**: Wildcards cannot be used at the start of a search term or when searching for phrases within quotes. #### Special Characters The following characters have a special meaning when they appear in a query: + - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ \* ? : / To instruct Search to interpret any of these characters literally, rather as a special character, precede the character with a backslash character **\** For example, the term *web -based* will search for *web NOT base* so either remove the space before - or escape it **web \-based** to find web-based documents. Another example, *complexity n^2* is best to be searched with escaping **complexity n\^2** as ^ is interpreted as boost a term.

applications.content: City project # How a technology museum will elevate Bengalaru’s innovation story ## Project: building a ‘Museum of Innovation, Start-Up and Technology’ Last updated: Fri 17 October 2025 By WCCF Editor **The Purpose** Bengaluru, as a leading tech hub, is the perfect location for a museum that honours India’s tech pioneers. The museum will showcase the rich history of Indian technology, solidifying Bengaluru’s position as an industry leader. Its purpose is to build India’s first phygital tech museum showcasing the city’s journey as a tech hub – its past, present and future. applications.title: Startup Museum Planned in Bengaluru with Grand Egyptian Museum Architects – GKToday
applications.content: # Startup Museum Planned in Bengaluru with Grand Egyptian Museum Architects July 22, 2026 The Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology (MIST) is a planned museum in Bengaluru, Karnataka, and it is legally registered as the Karnataka Technology Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF). The project is being developed as a public-private partnership between the UnboxingBLR Foundation and the Karnataka Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology (ITBT). #### Project Structure and Ownership MIST is structured as a public-private partnership with a 51% stake held by the UnboxingBLR Foundation and a 49% stake held by the Karnataka ITBT Department. The museum is intended to present India’s journey in innovation, startups, and technology through a dedicated institutional framework. #### Architectural Design and Selection Process The Heneghan Peng Architects Consortium won the bid to design MIST on 21 July 2026. The consortium was selected through a two-stage global Quality and Cost-Based Selection process from six shortlisted consortia. The Dublin-based consortium is known for designing the Grand Egyptian Museum, and it includes Bengaluru-based Cadence Architects in its team. #### Location and Associated Institutions MIST and Innoverse are twin institutions being developed within the repurposed Switchgear Factory Shed at the NGEF campus in Bengaluru. Innoverse is planned as a hub for incubating startups and fostering partnerships under the Karnataka ITBT Department. > #### Important Facts for Exams > > * The Grand Egyptian Museum is located near the Giza pyramids in Egypt and is one of the largest archaeological museums in the world. > * Quality and Cost-Based Selection is a procurement method used in public projects to assess both technical quality and financial bid value. > * Public-private partnership models are used in India for infrastructure, education, transport, and cultural projects. > * Bengaluru is a major Indian centre for information technology, startups, and biotechnology. #### Timeline and Development Phases Phase 1 of MIST is targeted for completion in 2028. Earlier planning references had indicated a phase one opening in 2027 and a phase two completion in 2028. **Category:** Science & Technology ### Leave a Reply Cancel reply

applications.title: Karnataka to build India’s first Museum of Innovation, Startups, Technology in Bengaluru
applications.content: Karnataka # Karnataka to build India’s first Museum of Innovation, Startups, Technology in Bengaluru He said that the Innoverse Foundation is a state government initiative to position Karnataka as a global DeepTech capital. Home Minister Priyank Kharge.File Photo | Express Express News Service Updated on: 25 Jul 2026, 2:15 am BENGALURU: Karnataka will set up India’s first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology (MIST) on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model at Rs 300 crore, Minister for Home, Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Priyank Kharge, said on Friday. The minister announced that the museum would be set up at the repurposed Switchgear Factory Shed in NGEF in the city. The announcement was part of a slew of initiatives, including the Innoverse Foundation, increase in grant for deep-tech startups to Rs 1 crore under Elevate Next, a proposed AI University and others ahead of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), that will be held at Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) from November 17 to 19, with the theme-- ‘AI & Beyond’. He said MIST will be a joint initiative between the UnboxingBLR Foundation and the Karnataka Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology and added that they have selected the Henegan Peng Architects consortium, a globally renowned firm behind the Grand Egyptian Museum. He said that the Innoverse Foundation is a state government initiative to position Karnataka as a global DeepTech capital. “Innoverse acts as a catalyst, mentoring successful revenue-generating deep-tech Startups to evolve from good product-market fit to industry dominance. The Foundation empowers the next generation of industry leaders by providing critical market access, access to essential capital, and expert mentorship”, he said. applications.content: Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation reposted this Recently reviewed the progress of #INNOVERSE and the Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology #MIST. These are two transformative, government-backed deep-tech and cultural initiatives being developed in Bengaluru. Conceived as complementary institutions, both projects are being delivered through a pioneering Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model between the IT BT Department, Karnataka and UnboxingBLR. The Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology will be India’s first museum dedicated exclusively to documenting the nation’s remarkable journey in innovation, technology and entrepreneurship. Rooted in India’s present and inspired by its future, MIST will showcase the ideas, institutions and innovators that have transformed the country’s technological landscape while inspiring curiosity, creativity and conversation across generations. The museum is being developed by the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation and will be located within the historic NGEF Campus at Baiyappanahalli, occupying one of the original switchgear factory sheds nestled within a 105-acre campus that includes 65 acres of urban forest. Through the adaptive reuse of this industrial heritage structure, the existing 10,061 sq. m. footprint will be expanded to nearly 24,000 sq. m. by adding new floors and double-height volumes. Approximately 12,325 sq. m. will be dedicated to immersive museum galleries and public experiences, creating a landmark institution that celebrates India’s innovation journey while preserving an important chapter of Karnataka’s industrial heritage.

applications.content: # Bengaluru to Host India’s First Startup Tech Museum by 2027. Bengaluru, India’s startup capital, is set to add another feather to its innovation crown with the announcement of the country’s first Startup & Tech Museum, slated to open by 2027. According to Deccan Herald , the museum will span 12,000 sqm at the repurposed Switch Gear factory shed on the NGEF campus in Baiyappanahalli. Developed under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Department of Electronics, IT&BT, and UnboxingBLR, the initiative will be managed by the Karnataka Technology and Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF). This museum aims to showcase India’s entrepreneurial journey, technological breakthroughs, and startup milestones, offering visitors an immersive experience into the country’s innovation ecosystem. Beyond being a cultural landmark, it will serve as an educational hub—inspiring students, founders, and investors by chronicling the stories of India’s most impactful startups. For Bengaluru, already home to thousands of startups and global R&D centers, the museum reinforces its identity as the epicenter of India’s innovation economy. By 2027, this space will not only celebrate past achievements but also act as a living lab for future ideas, bridging history with aspiration. India’s startup story deserves a stage, and Bengaluru is building it. #StartupIndia #InnovationEconomy #BengaluruStartups #TechMuseum #India2030 #Entrepreneurship #KTIMF #PublicPrivatePartnership #NationBuilding
